components.gap: The chapter defines coherence as avoiding a Dutch book and refers the reader to chapter 4.1 (Hajek & Staffel) (held PDF p. 278). The handbook has that linked unit (handbook/parts/p15/rationality-4-1.tex:81-106, sec:p15-rationality-4-1, Dutch books, their objections to the betting identification, and the finite equivalence thm:p17-finite-price-coherence). rationality-4-4.tex never compares its conditional-event coherence (two-sided precise prices, called-off bets, coherence only on the active union, lines 41-69) with that treatment. Its comparison list (lines 800-838) covers finite probability, Bayes, lower previsions, PCTL, P08 System P and P13 Abelard but omits the Dutch-book unit. The 4.1 objections (no unique two-sided price, stake effects, utility of money) are not kept against the two-sided-stake assumption at lines 55-58; only the one-sided lower-prevision contrast (lines 817-823) touches them. No reverse comparison exists either: rationality-4-1.tex does not reference sec:p15-rationality-4-4. The comparisons with 4.6 and 6.2 exist from the P19 side (rationality-4-6.tex:144,445; rationality-6-2.tex:42,274,471).
